sources.name: Petrosino et al.
sources.text: "Scared Straight" and Other Juvenile Awareness Programs, Campbell/Cochrane systematic review (2013): 9 randomized trials, OR 1.68 (95% CI 1.20 to 2.36), crime increased 1% to 28%, harm robust to removing the Finckenauer study; the 41% vs 11% figures as reported.

sources.name: US National Institute of Justice
sources.text: CrimeSolutions practice profile, Juvenile Awareness Programs (Scared Straight): rated "Ineffective"; the evaluation found participation increases the odds of future offending.

sources.name: Office of Justice Programs
sources.text: abstracts, Scared Straight: The Myth That Roared and Scared Straight! and the Panacea Phenomenon (Finckenauer): the 80 to 90% claim, the Lifers'-Group-and-county-judge survey with no follow-up or record of non-replies, the 38-state spread.

sources.name: UK College of Policing
sources.text: Crime Reduction Toolkit, "Scared Straight programmes" (first published 19 Feb 2015; PDF saved by the author and read directly): rates the effect "very strong" evidence of an overall rise in crime. Citing Petrosino et al. 2013 (9 studies): after accounting for bias, reoffending was 68% higher among participants than non-participants, higher in 7 of 9 studies. Citing Aos et al. 2006: net cost to the taxpayer of $14,667 per participant, after accounting for the cost of the additional crimes the programme caused. Conclusion: "a backfire effect of the programme."

sources.name: Variety
sources.text: Beyond Scared Straight review, confirmed by direct fetch: A&E, premiered Thursday, Jan. 13, 2011, 10 p.m., 90 minutes; produced by Arnold Shapiro Prods., the original 1978 film's own producer.

sources.name: Hollywood Reporter
sources.text: Hollywood Flashback (2018), confirmed by direct fetch: Scared Straight! "went on to win an Academy Award for feature documentary," unusual since it lacked the theatrical release the Academy then preferred.

sources.name: Robinson and Slowikowski
sources.text: Baltimore Sun op-ed (Jan 31, 2011), confirmed by direct fetch: authors Laurie O. Robinson (Assistant Attorney General, Office of Justice Programs) and Jeff Slowikowski (Acting Administrator, Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention): "scared straight is not only ineffective but is potentially harmful"; "the study strongly suggested the program caused harm."

sources.name: US DOJ COPS Office
sources.text: publication on juvenile awareness programs: the film's 9-of-10 claim, congressional hearings, randomization caveats in Finckenauer and Yarborough.
